meta.title: TYPO3 agent readiness — what the stack offers AI agents | nr-llm
meta.description: What TYPO3 Core, official add-ons, Netresearch extensions and community extensions offer AI agents: content for agents, external agents, agents inside TYPO3, control and coding agents.

hero.headline: TYPO3 agent readiness
hero.tagline: What the TYPO3 stack offers AI agents today, and who provides each part.

intro: An agent that works with a website needs more than a language model. It needs content it can read, an interface it may call, rights that limit what it does, and a review step before anything goes live. This page lists what exists for each of these in TYPO3 Core, in official add-ons, in Netresearch extensions and in other community extensions.
Each row names its origin and links its source. Capabilities that are documented but not yet released are left out or named as work in progress.

origins.heading: Who provides what
origins.intro: The table rows use five origin categories. Netresearch's open-source extensions are part of the TYPO3 ecosystem as well; the categories show who delivers which part of a solution.

items.body: Core and the system extensions shipped with it. Some must be activated and configured.
Offerings of the TYPO3 project or the TYPO3 Company that are separate from Core, such as the TYPO3 Suite or the Dev Companion.
Open-source extensions developed by Netresearch, such as nr-llm, Cowriter or nr-browser-ai.
Extensions by other agencies and developers, credited by name.
Selecting, connecting and configuring the parts for a concrete installation: permissions, models, data sources, approvals, quality checks and operation.

sections.heading: What TYPO3 Core brings as a foundation
sections.intro: Core provides the structures an agent that works under control needs: typed records, permissions, drafts and integration points. The LLM, MCP, WebMCP and A2A functions come from the extensions further down.

rows.detail: TCA describes tables, fields and relations. Every write to a TCA table goes through DataHandler, which evaluates the acting user's write permissions.

Backend groups limit which tables can be read or modified, which page-tree branches and file mounts are reachable, and which languages can be edited. An agent that acts as a backend user inherits these limits.
Changes stay as versioned drafts that can be previewed and pass review stages before they are published. An agent can prepare a draft while review and publication stay in the editorial process.
TYPO3 integrates the Symfony Messenger message bus. Messages are handled synchronously by default.
rows.limit: Asynchronous processing needs routing to a transport (Core ships a Doctrine transport) and a running messenger:consume worker.

rows.detail: Reactions receive webhooks from external systems. Webhooks notify external systems when TYPO3 events occur.
Each form is stored as a structured definition of elements, options, validators and finishers. nr-browser-ai derives browser tools from these definitions (see below).
TYPO3 14 introduced a modernized translation workflow in which translation services can be plugged in as localization handlers.
rows.limit: The handler API is still marked internal in TYPO3 14.3 and may change.

sections.heading: Making content readable for LLMs and external agents
sections.intro: llms.txt, Markdown versions of pages, structured data and JSON output give agents a representation of the site they can use directly.

rows.capability: Provide llms.txt and agent skills from configuration
rows.detail: Writes /llms.txt from a file or inline text in the site configuration, at deploy time as a static file. Optionally also writes /.well-known/agent-skills.json when skills are configured.
rows.limit: One docroot gets one file: in a multi-site instance the first site's configuration is used. agent-skills.json is a concrete interface, not a widely supported standard.

rows.capability: Generate llms.txt from the page tree
rows.detail: Builds llms.txt from the page tree with configurable depth and page-type exclusions, skips hidden, restricted and no-index pages, serves pages as Markdown and exports them via CLI.
Generates llms.txt with Markdown access to page content and can protect these endpoints with an API key.

rows.component: b13/ai-bots-love-markdown by b13; used in the Netresearch demo
rows.detail: Serves a page as Markdown on Accept: text/markdown or via a URL suffix, with page metadata as front matter and a rel="alternate" link for discovery.
Adds schema.org structured data to pages as JSON-LD, so content types and relations are machine-readable.

rows.component: friendsoftypo3/headless by the TYPO3 Headless initiative
rows.detail: Renders pages, content elements, menus and metadata as JSON, with multilingual handling and workspace preview.

Shows or hides pages and content depending on configurable contexts, including one that matches requests from known AI crawlers. Cowriter can create audience variants that are bound to such a context.
rows.limit: The User-Agent is set by the client, so the AI-crawler context classifies requests; it does not authenticate them.

notes: The Netresearch TYPO3 demo serves a hand-curated llms.txt directly from nginx and offers every page as Markdown via b13/ai-bots-love-markdown. It does not use nr-wellknown.

llms.txt is a proposal for giving agents a curated overview of a site. It does not guarantee that content is used or ranked by AI systems; Markdown and structured data are representations agents can use directly.

sections.heading: External agents can work with TYPO3
sections.intro: Browser tools, CMS tools and delegated tasks are three different capabilities. Each one has its own interface and its own limits.

rows.detail: Answers questions about the open page with Gemini Nano through Chrome's built-in Prompt API, on the visitor's device.
rows.limit: Runs only where the browser offers the Prompt API. WebLLM was evaluated and not adopted.

rows.component: nr-browser-ai on top of the form system extension
rows.detail: Generates a JSON Schema from a form definition and registers the form as a tool with the browser's model context (WebMCP) where the browser supports it. The tool fills the visible form and queries the form's configured data source.
rows.limit: It does not submit the form, run finishers or execute anything on the server. For multi-step forms only the first page is described.

rows.detail: Gives MCP clients the page tree and workspace-capable tables with schema inspection over an OAuth-protected HTTP endpoint. Record changes are queued in a workspace.
rows.limit: It uses the user's first writable workspace. Uploaded files land in storage immediately, because files are not workspace-versioned.

rows.capability: Use external MCP tools inside TYPO3
rows.detail: Administrators connect external MCP servers. Imported tools start disabled, are enabled one by one and by default need human approval per call.
rows.limit: The client speaks HTTP (no stdio) and passes on text results only.

rows.capability: Address TYPO3 as an A2A agent
rows.detail: TYPO3 answers A2A 1.0 requests over JSON-RPC and publishes an Agent Card with the skills of administrator-defined profiles. Registered clients authenticate with a token, follow task status, answer follow-up questions, cancel tasks and fetch results. Each client's tasks run as a dedicated non-admin backend user in a configured workspace.
rows.limit: Files are off by default. When enabled, a task accepts files from the client. Returning a FAL file additionally needs the profile's approval of its clients as recipients and a tool that ships disabled; only files the client's backend user may read are sent.

rows.capability: Delegate work to other A2A agents
rows.detail: Administrators register remote A2A agents. The skills on their Agent Card become tools that are off by default and by default need approval before a run delegates.
rows.limit: The client exchanges text only. While the backend chat nr-mcp-agent is installed, agent runs are not offered delegation tools yet (see the limits section).

rows.capability: Personal agents with the editor's own rights
rows.detail: Where an administrator allows it, editors issue their own revocable A2A tokens, limited to permitted profiles, by default to a draft workspace and an expiry. Every request is checked against the editor's current groups.

rows.capability: Official API for records and files
rows.detail: A REST API for records and files with OAuth 2.0 or static tokens. Each app is limited to its backend user's rights and to the actions it is allowed.
rows.limit: Part of the TYPO3 Suite, a commercial offering of the TYPO3 Company. An MCP server for the Suite is announced without a launch date.

notes: The Netresearch TYPO3 demo answers the A2A protocol since 17 November 2026. Its agent card is public; tasks need an administrator-issued token, and writes go to a draft workspace after approval.

sections.heading: Agents and workflows inside TYPO3
sections.intro: nr-llm runs agents within TYPO3 itself: with CMS context, tools, follow-up questions and approvals.

rows.detail: Runs are stored, can run in a background worker and keep a timeline of their tool calls.
A run can pause for an approval or a typed answer and then continue, be rejected or be cancelled.
Built-in read tools cover content, page tree, TCA and FlexForm schemas, TypoScript and TSconfig, files and diagnostics. Each tool and each group can be switched off.

rows.component: Write tools in nr-llm, DataHandler and workspaces
rows.detail: Writing tools ship disabled and every call pauses for a human approval. Record writers go through DataHandler into the run's workspace.
rows.limit: Not every writing tool uses a workspace: cache clearing and the redirect tools are admin-only, and redirects are written live.

rows.detail: SKILL.md instructions are versioned and approved; a configuration loads them always or on demand. nr-llm never executes scripts a skill references.

rows.capability: Central rules for language and style
rows.detail: Personas, tone, audience and style are kept as reusable building blocks that extensions combine by tag.
Returns cited site content from the installed search index (EXT:solr, ke_search or indexed_search) or from a database fallback.
An action can run over a folder or a page tree. Each proposed change waits on its own approval card.
Returns typed yes/no, choice or score decisions. Thresholds and consequences stay in the calling code.
Schema-validated JSON output on every supported provider, plus shared services for translation, vision, image generation, embeddings and speech.

sections.heading: Applications built on this foundation
sections.intro: Netresearch extensions that use nr-llm for concrete editorial and site tasks, plus the integration of community AI extensions.

rows.detail: A CKEditor assistant that improves, summarizes, extends, corrects and translates text, suggests page fields including SEO and social texts, generates alt texts and, optionally, images and audience variants.
A backend chat on nr-llm's agent runtime with persistent conversations, nr-llm tools, background processing and guided flows such as fixing missing alt texts.
Answers visitor questions only from the site's own indexed pages. Each search or chat element can be limited to one page subtree.
rows.limit: The demo's extension-advisor chat is not publicly accessible, so that anonymous visitors cannot start paid model calls.

rows.detail: Turns a web page or PDF into one content brief and from it into formats such as a podcast, a diagram, a story carousel, a summary, an FAQ, social posts, a newsletter, a slide deck and a handout.
rows.limit: Approved social posts can be handed to an automation tool through a webhook, optionally signed; other formats are not sent by webhook.

rows.detail: A backend wizard: pick a template, answer briefing questions, review generated page fields and content sections, then choose where in the page tree the page is created. Templates limit which content elements may be generated.

rows.capability: Bring community AI extensions under shared control
rows.detail: Routes the LLM calls of supported extensions, among them AI SEO Helper, T3AI, AI File Metadata, Texter, Exception Solver and Sitescore, through nr-llm and its policies.
rows.limit: Each integration is off by default and activates only for a supported version whose code contract still matches.

rows.component: Autotranslate by Thiele & Klose with nr-llm
rows.detail: Autotranslate translates pages and content, including scheduled batch jobs. With nr-llm as its translation backend it can use DeepL or a language model, with usage tracking and budgets.
rows.limit: Autotranslate 3.6 and earlier need an upstream change applied as a patch.

rows.capability: A curated combination of the stack
rows.detail: A Composer metapackage that installs Netresearch AI extensions in versions tested together. CI installs it and opens each extension's backend modules.
rows.limit: The edition pins the versions that passed its compatibility run; newer single releases, including nr-llm's A2A features, are not part of it yet. The run does not test model answers.

notes: Other agencies offer their own AI foundations: b13 AiM is a central AI layer that selects providers and models, enforces rules and tracks costs; NITSAN's T3AF is an open-source foundation with a built-in MCP server, provider management, budgets and permissions.

sections.heading: What keeps the stack controllable
sections.intro: Which tasks a site can hand to an agent depends on how the task is limited, how its result is checked and who decides on publication.

rows.detail: Shared configuration for providers and models with criteria-based routing, fallback chains and local models via Ollama.
Per-user budgets cap requests, tokens and cost per day and per month.

rows.capability: Limit the scope of a task
rows.detail: A run can be bound to pages, records, tables and languages. DataHandler writes outside that scope are refused, for administrators too.

rows.component: Editorial profile in nr-llm with Core workspaces
rows.detail: A configuration can require that every change is written as a draft in a workspace, administrators included, and that a second person approves.
An optional second model checks finished texts against written rules and either reports or blocks violations.
rows.limit: Off by default; what it catches depends on the configured rules and model.

rows.detail: Golden prompt sets measure answer quality and flag regressions after changes to prompts, models or configuration.

rows.component: AI-written marker in nr-llm; optional b13/ai-label by b13
rows.detail: Pages and content elements written by a run are marked as AI-written. b13's ai-label adds AI-origin labels, a review record and a visible marker for visitors.
rows.limit: A technical approval is not an editorial review of the content.

rows.detail: How long conversations, agent runs, approvals and other data are kept is configurable per data category.
Stores secrets with envelope encryption, per-secret access by backend group, a tamper-evident audit log and rotation of secrets and the master key.
Adds SSRF protection to TYPO3's RequestFactory: it blocks private, loopback and metadata destinations, checks DNS results and redirects, and pins connections to verified addresses.
rows.limit: Direct cURL calls and other HTTP clients are not covered.

sections.heading: TYPO3 for coding agents
sections.intro: Agent readiness also covers development: coding agents that build and maintain TYPO3 projects need version-specific knowledge and runtime context.

rows.detail: A local MCP server that gives coding agents version-specific TYPO3 knowledge and read-only context from the local installation, plus task skills for common development work.
rows.limit: Experimental 0.x release. It writes nothing into the installation.

rows.detail: Every manual on docs.typo3.org gets an llms.txt; depending on the render it also gets Markdown pages and JSON indexes.
rows.limit: This applies to the documentation platform, not to TYPO3 websites.

rows.detail: A development-only bridge to Symfony AI Mate with diagnostic tools, nearly all read-only, for TYPO3's resolved runtime state such as TCA, TypoScript, Fluid, dependency injection and events.
rows.limit: The tools are called on demand through a CLI; there is no long-running server process.

limits.heading: Where the edges are today
limits.intro: These limits apply to the current releases. Work that is merged but not released is not counted as available.
items: The chain from the backend chat to a remote agent and back is not available yet. While nr-mcp-agent is installed, nr-llm offers agent runs no delegation tools. nr-mcp-agent already contains a display for a step that waits for a remote agent; it stays unreachable until nr-llm lifts this block. Keeping the final answer of such a step is in progress in nr-llm.
The A2A client exchanges text only. The A2A server accepts and returns files only when files are enabled.
nr-browser-ai is a proof of concept. Its form tools fill a form and query its data source; they never submit it.
nr-mcp-agent is published as a proof of concept; nr-repurpose and nr-http-guard are alpha releases.
llms.txt, Markdown and JSON output make content usable for agents. They do not guarantee that an AI system uses or ranks it.
Automated checks of the AI Edition install the extensions and open their modules; they do not judge model answers. An approval in a workspace is a technical step, not an editorial review.
